subject: English
title: English 4 (PECTAA, SNC 2020)
questions: How many Rashidun (rightly-guided) caliphs ruled the first caliphate?
The Rashidun Caliphate was ruled by four caliphs: Hazrat Abu Bakr, Hazrat Umar, Hazrat Usman and Hazrat Ali.
For how many years did the Rashidun Caliphate last?
The lesson says the Rashidun Caliphate lasted for 30 years.
What was the real name of Hazrat Abu Bakr Siddique?
His name was Abdullah; Abu Bakr was his kuniyyat and Siddique was his title.
Who was the first among men to accept Islam?
Hazrat Abu Bakr was the first among men to accept Islam.
Who was elected as the first caliph of Islam?
After the death of Rasoolullah (PBUH), Hazrat Abu Bakr was elected as the first caliph.
Which title was given to Hazrat Umar?
Hazrat Umar was given the title 'Farooq', the one who distinguishes between right and wrong.
For about how long did Hazrat Umar serve as caliph?
Hazrat Umar served Islam and the Muslims as caliph for ten and a half years.
Why was Hazrat Usman known as 'Ghani'?
He was a rich trader who spent generously in the way of Allah, so he was called Ghani.
Hazrat Usman married two daughters of the Holy Prophet (PBUH), so he was called Zun Noorain, holder of two lights.
Who was the first among children to accept Islam?
Hazrat Ali was the first among children to accept Islam, at about ten years of age.
Hazrat Ali is also known as:
Because he was very courageous, Hazrat Ali is known as 'the Lion of Allah'.
Which caliph was the third caliph of Islam?
After the martyrdom of Hazrat Umar, Hazrat Usman became the third caliph.
How many vowel letters are there in the English alphabet?
The lesson says there are five vowels: a, e, i, o and u.
A group of two letters that makes a single sound is called a:
A digraph is a group of two letters that makes one sound, e.g. 'ch' in chick.
Which of these is an uncountable noun?
Uncountable nouns have no plural form, e.g. water, weather, furniture.
In the word 'lamb', which letter is silent?
In 'lamb' the letter b is written but not pronounced.
Who wrote the poem 'Caterpillar' in Unit 2?
The poem 'Caterpillar' in this unit is by Christina Rossetti.
In the poem, how is the caterpillar described?
The poem begins: 'Brown and furry, Caterpillar in a hurry'.
Where is the caterpillar walking to in the poem?
To the shady leaf or stalk
The poet asks the caterpillar to take its walk to the shady leaf or stalk.
A caterpillar is a stage in the life cycle of a butterfly.
to stay in the air in one place
In the vocabulary list, hover means to stay in the air in one place.
the main stem of a plant
The vocabulary list gives stalk as the main stem of a plant.
In which word is the letter 'w' silent?
In 'wrap' the w is not pronounced.
A word that refers to a group of people or things is called a:
A collective noun refers to a group, e.g. a team of players, a herd of deer.
Choose the correct collective noun: a ___ of flowers.
We say a bouquet of flowers.
Choose the correct article: She is ___ honest girl.
The 'h' in honest is silent, so the word starts with a vowel sound and takes 'an'.
In 'Shazia eats Australian apples', the word 'Australian' is an adjective of:
An adjective of origin tells where something comes from, e.g. Chinese, Turkish, Australian.
In Mahnoor's story, how did she make people care about plants and insects?
Her mother suggested a colourful chart; Mahnoor and her friends made charts and put them up.
In its raw form, chocolate comes from:
The lesson says chocolate comes from cocoa trees in its raw form.
Where do the flowers of a cocoa tree grow?
Surprisingly, cocoa flowers grow on the trunk of the tree, not on its branches.
How many beans does each cocoa pod contain?
How long does a cocoa pod take to ripen?
It takes the pod about six months to ripen.
Who brought chocolate to Spain in the 1500s?
Chocolate came from Central and South America to Spain through Spanish explorers.
In ancient times, chocolate was a symbol of:
Only the rich could afford it, so chocolate was a symbol of wealth.
The edible pieces left after removing the shells of roasted beans are called:
After the shells are removed, the remaining edible pieces are called nibs.
What is added to the nib paste besides sugar?
The nibs are mixed with sugar; dried milk and some flavours are then added.
What should we always do after eating chocolate?
The lesson reminds us to always brush our teeth after eating chocolate.
A combination of two vowel sounds in a single syllable is called a:
A diphthong begins with one vowel sound and moves to another, e.g. coil, pain, now.
A pie chart is used to:
The lesson says a pie chart compares parts of a whole, while a bar graph compares different groups.
Joining (transition) words connect one sentence or paragraph to the next.
Where did the class go on their historical trip?
The children took the school bus for a trip to the Pakistan Army Museum, Lahore.
Why did Tashif collect pictures about the Pakistan Army?
His uncle was an army officer
It was his hobby, as his uncle was an army officer.
How many Nishan-e-Haider heroes did the children want to meet in the museum?
They waited to meet the eleven heroes from the armed forces who laid down their lives.
The teacher told them Nishan-e-Haider means 'Mark of the Lion'.
It is the highest military award, given for an extraordinary act of bravery in which the soldier gives his life.
What did the children see on entering the museum building?
Inside the museum they saw four captured Indian tanks with a brief history.
The 'Rebirth of the Nation' gallery showed the Quaid-e-Azam addressing the assembly on:
It had a life-size portrait of the Quaid addressing the assembly of Pakistan on August 11, 1947.
For about how long did the children explore the museum?
The narrator explored the museum with classmates for more than three hours.
In 'play' the sound changes from one vowel to another in one syllable, so it is a diphthong.
Why are soldiers called our national heroes?
They sacrifice their lives to guard the country
The lesson describes heroes who laid down their lives to guard the sacred land of Pakistan.
Which noun has the same form in singular and plural?
Some nouns do not change in the plural, e.g. 'The sheep are grazing in the field.'
Words with opposite meanings are called:
Antonyms are words with opposite meanings; synonyms have similar meanings.
Who wrote the poem 'Thank You, Lord'?
The poem 'Thank You, Lord' is by Mary Fairchild.
How does the poet start each day?
By taking a moment to bow and pray
'Lord, in the morning I start each day, by taking a moment to bow and pray.'
What does the poet start her prayer with?
'I start with thanks, and then give praise for all your kind and loving ways.'
What will the poet do when sunshine turns to rain?
She says she won't doubt or hide in fear, because God is with her.
Until when will the poet keep God close in sight?
Until she crawls into bed at night
'And I will keep you close in sight until I crawl in bed tonight.'
A group of two or three consonants in a word, each keeping its sound, is called a:
In a consonant cluster each consonant keeps its own sound, e.g. 'str' in street.
In 'Getting Started', why is cutting trees wrong?
The tree in the picture says, 'Please, don't kill me! I give you oxygen.'
Which place did Mahira and Aqsa visit in the dialogue?
Mahira asks Aqsa whether she enjoyed the visit to the Faisal Masjid.
Words that sound the same but have different meanings and spellings are called:
Homophones sound alike but differ in meaning and spelling, e.g. sea/see.
King is masculine; its feminine gender noun is queen.
Where did Rehan find his friend Sa'ad sitting alone?
On a bench in a park
One evening Rehan found Sa'ad sitting alone on a bench in a park.
He had been rude to a classmate
Sa'ad was ashamed of being rude to a classmate who limped while walking.
What was the name of the boy Sa'ad was rude to?
Sa'ad made fun of Faraz, who limped while walking.
Faraz had been selected in the team as a:
Sa'ad, the captain, was shocked that Faraz had been selected as wicket keeper.
What happened to Faraz because of Sa'ad's rude behaviour?
Faraz was so depressed by the rude behaviour that he left school.
What did Rehan advise Sa'ad to do?
Go to Faraz's house and say sorry
Rehan said it was not too late and told Sa'ad to go and apologise.
How did Faraz respond to Sa'ad's apology?
Faraz was a good boy; he forgave Sa'ad and hugged him at once.
What is the main lesson of 'Valuing Others'?
Treat differently-abled people with kindness and respect
The story teaches that we must value others and never be rude to differently-abled people.
Before a vowel sound, 'the' is pronounced as:
'The' is pronounced 'thee' before a vowel sound (the apple) and 'thuh' before a consonant sound.
Which phrase is a polite way to seek permission?
'May I borrow ...?' politely asks permission before using someone else's things.
Which languages are spoken in Punjab according to the lesson?
The lesson says that in Punjab people speak Punjabi and Seraiki.
Shina, Balti and Burushaski are regional languages of:
In Gilgit-Baltistan, Shina, Balti and Burushaski are regional languages.
The Sindhi cap and ajrak are part of the traditional dress of:
The Sindhi cap and ajrak are part of men's dress in Sindh.
Which festival in Balochistan attracts people from all across the country?
In Balochistan, the Sibi Festival attracts people from all across the country.
Hospitality, hard work and bravery are distinctive features of:
Hospitality, hard work and bravery are features of Pakhtunwali, the Pakhtun way of life.
Which is a prominent traditional dress of Kashmiri men and women?
Phiran is a prominent traditional dress of Kashmiri men and women.
Which festival is celebrated every year in Kashmir?
The lesson says Pirchinasi is celebrated every year in Kashmir.
Sindhi culture is dominated by great:
Sindhi culture is dominated by great Sufis, mystics and martyrs.
Poetry and storytelling are very popular among the:
The lesson says poetry and storytelling are very popular among the Baloch.
Pakhtun men often wear a turban or a:
Pakhtun men usually wear shalwar kameez, a waistcoat and a turban or a pakol hat.
In 'He is playing', the verb 'is' is used as a:
When be, do or have are used with a main verb, they are helping verbs.
In 'You are late', the verb 'are' is used as a:
When be, do or have are used alone without another verb, they are main verbs.
Who asked the children to make a poster about good study habits?
Miss Hina told them to make a poster about good study habits.
When the poster was completed, it was displayed in the classroom.
Which of these is a good study habit from the poster?
The poster lists: set your goals, make a timetable, make notes and revise classwork.
What result did the narrator get after adopting good study habits?
In the final term the narrator got first position in the class.
To whom did the narrator write the invitation letter?
The invitation begins 'Dear Asif' and is signed 'Your cousin'.
The invitation says the party was on Friday evening at the narrator's house.
In the dialogue, what had the son forgotten?
That he had a test tomorrow
He had been playing for two hours and forgot he had a test the next day.
What does Baba advise his son?
There is a time for play and a time for study
Baba says there is a time for play and a time for study, and things should be done on time.
'His' shows possession (his book); he, they and we are subject pronouns.
Who wrote the poem 'Whole Duty of Children'?
'Whole Duty of Children' is by Robert Louis Stevenson.
According to the poem, a child should always say:
'A child should always say what's true.'
When should a child speak, according to the poem?
'And speak when he is spoken to.'
Where should a child behave mannerly, according to the poem?
'And behave mannerly at table, at least as far as he is able.'
The poem 'Whole Duty of Children' is mainly about:
The poem talks about good manners a child should follow.
Why did Mama ask Sidra to take a bath before breakfast?
To take care of personal hygiene
Because she was late for school
Mama says, 'We should always take care of our personal hygiene.'
In the word 'helped', the -ed ending sounds like:
After p, k, sh, ch, s and f, the -ed ending sounds like 't' (helped, thanked).
In the word 'wanted', the -ed ending sounds like:
After t or d, the -ed ending is pronounced 'id' (wanted, needed).
A table of contents helps us to:
The table of contents helps us to find the chapters in a book.
We should wash our hands with soap:
The lesson reminds us to wash hands before and after a meal.
Choose the correct word: We ___ speak rudely to our elders.
We should not speak rudely to our elders; 'should not' shows something we must avoid.
Choose the correct word: You ___ go to school on time.
'Should' is used for advice or duty: you should go to school on time.
What did Sara bring home in 'Be Aware, Be Safe'?
Mother asks Sara, 'Who gave you this doll?'
Sara says there was a man in the street who gave it.
What did Mother say about accepting gifts from strangers?
It is fine if they smile
Mother says it is not good to accept gifts from strangers because it might be dangerous.
If a stranger offers you a ride, a toy or candy, you should:
Mother says to say 'No!', walk away quickly and tell her or Baba.
What did Sara and Ahsan promise their mother?
To share all their activities with her
Sara promises, 'I will share all my activities with you.'
Why should we not be friendly with strangers?
Mother explains that it might be dangerous for children.
Sara's brother in the lesson is named:
Sara and her brother Ahsan entered their home.
Past tense of regular verbs is formed by adding:
Regular verbs form their past tense by adding -d or -ed, e.g. play-played.
Adverbs of time (today, yesterday, soon) tell us when an action happens.
Which sentence is in the future tense?
The future tense shows actions that will happen, using 'will'.
How did the fox serve soup to the stork?
In a bowl with a lid
The cunning fox served the soup in flat plates.
Why could the stork not eat from the flat dish?
The stork's beak was so long that he could not sip from the flat dish.
How did the stork serve the meal to the fox?
In a jar with a narrow neck
The stork served the meal in a jar with a narrow neck.
What did the stork tell the fox at the end?
Do not ridicule or degrade anyone; Allah has made us all equal
The stork said calmly, 'Do not ridicule or degrade anyone... Allah has made us all equal.'
The fox said sorry and they became friends
The fox was ashamed, said sorry, and they became friends.
What kind of animal was the fox in the story?
The fox always teased others and played a trick on the stork.
In which type of sentence does our voice rise at the end?
In yes-no questions such as 'Do you obey traffic signs?' the voice rises at the end.
In a wh-question like 'What is your name?' the voice usually:
In wh-questions the voice falls on the final stressed syllable.
An apostrophe replaces the missing letter: do not becomes don't.
I am becomes I'm; the apostrophe stands for the missing 'a'.
What did Ahsan's teacher give him?
Ahsan's teacher gave him a brochure on traffic rules and road safety.
What problem did Ahsan see in front of his school?
Ahsan said there is always a traffic jam in front of his school.
Why did people not follow traffic rules near Ahsan's school?
There was no traffic police on that road
Ahsan never saw traffic police there, so nobody followed the rules.
To whom did Ahsan write the letter?
With his father's help, Ahsan wrote to the Inspector General, Traffic Police Headquarters, Islamabad.
Where should we cross the road?
The brochure says: cross only at the zebra crossing.
What should we do before crossing the road?
Look to the left and right
The brochure says look to your left and right before crossing the road.
While riding a motorbike or bicycle, we should wear a:
One of the brochure's rules is 'Wear a helmet'.
In a car, we should always:
The brochure says: fasten your seatbelt and sit quietly in the back seat.
Ahsan's father said helping the police by reporting traffic issues is our:
His father said, 'As a good citizen, it is our moral duty to help the police.'
Which sentence is in the past continuous tense?
Past continuous = was/were + verb-ing, for actions in progress in the past.
'Little Things' is by Julia A. Carney.
According to the poem, little drops of water make the:
'Little drops of water, little grains of sand, make the mighty ocean and the pleasant land.'
Little grains of sand make the:
The grains of sand make the pleasant land.
What makes our earth an Eden, according to the poem?
Little deeds of kindness and little words of love
'Little deeds of kindness, little words of love, make our earth an Eden.'
The main idea of 'Little Things' is that:
The poem teaches that little things are not useless; everything has its importance.
Little errors, according to the poem, lead the soul:
away from the path of virtue
'So the little errors lead the soul away from the path of virtue.'
Using body parts and gestures to communicate feelings is called:
Non-verbal communication uses body parts and gestures to show feelings and emotions.
The rise and fall of the voice while speaking is called:
Intonation is the rise and fall of the voice while speaking.
Which pair of words rhymes in the poem?
'Sand' and 'land' rhyme in the first stanza.
